answer: Age in the trust hierarchy is bought with per-identity verified output rather than with elapsed time, so an operator cannot batch his accounts through a queue and must run each one through genuine, individually verified work. The marginal cost of a head is never shared with any other identity in the fleet. The nectar is the attested output, the anchor the stranger who checks it, and the haven the tier the pair unlocks; the nectar is per identity, the anchor cannot be the farm's own, and the haven is what waiting alone cannot buy. Each head also needs a stranger to attest that work.
